title: finance/branches
description: One row per physical bank branch. The bank's offices. Every account is opened at a branch, so this is the table to join through for any question about regional performance or customer distribution.

id.description: Surrogate primary key, sequential from 1. Every other table joins against this.

branch_code.description: Four-digit office code, the same one that appears inside every IBAN opened at this branch. Spanish account numbers really do encode the office.

name.description: Branch name, combining the bank with the city and the district it serves. Entirely invented.

city.description: Spanish city the branch operates in, drawn from real municipalities weighted by population.

province.description: Province the branch sits in, always consistent with the first two digits of its postal code.

address.description: Street address in Spanish format, with the number after the street name. Invented.

postal_code.description: Spanish postal code whose leading pair encodes the province, so address validation passes on it.

phone.description: Branch telephone, with a dialling prefix that matches the province it is in.

opened_at.description: Date the branch began trading, spread across the four decades before the dataset period.
